changes.from: the corner of South Water and Clark streets

anchor_change.rule: THE PAPER'S OWN COLOPHON, TWICE, AND IT DOES NOT SAY THE SAME THING BOTH TIMES. 1834-01-07 c006 reads the Democrat's imprint 'in the building on the corner of South Water and Clark streets'; 1835-05-20 c007 reads the colophon of that issue 'over Messrs. Jones & King['s] Hard[ware store]', South Water street. Two different landmarks and not two spellings of one: 'the corner of South Water and Clark streets' is a platted crossing this project holds, and "Messrs. Jones & King's hardware store" is a house of business in the same street, carried in this corpus as business_jones_king_co. A printing office is not in a crossing and over a hardware store at the same time, so between 1834-01-07 and 1835-05-20 the office's printed address changed, and the corpus brackets the change by those two dates and no closer: no printing of this colophon between them has been read. THE CORPUS SAYS WHY, in the OTHER Democrat record rather than in this one — chicago_democrat_1834_10_08 c005 offers 'the store now occupied by W. Kimball, and as the office of the Democrat' for sale with possession in November 1834, which is a landlord's notice and not this shop's own reading, so it is cited here and claims no anchor here. The scene date is 1835-07-01, six weeks after the later colophon first ran, so the anchor live in the scene is the hardware store.
anchor_change.cannot_say: WHICH HOUSE, AND WHERE IN THE STREET. "Messrs. Jones & King's hardware store" is an anchor this corpus cannot resolve to ground: business_jones_king_co prints South Water Street and nothing narrower, and business_jones_king prints 'their store in Water-street, near the bridge', an anchor the committed town does not hold. So this rule moves the office OFF the corner of South Water and Clark streets and does not put it anywhere in particular — South Water Street, over a store whose own address the papers never fix. That is a loss of precision and it is the honest reading: the narrower address was the older one. NOR DOES IT SAY WHAT BECAME OF THE BUILDING. data/structures/chicago_democrat_office.json stands at the corner on the 26 November 1833 imprint and on Andreas, and a building does not move when its tenant does; nothing here touches its coordinate. WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN is whether 'over Jones & King's' is a separate building at all or the same corner block under a new ground-floor tenancy — c007 says 'over', which is a floor, and no printing reached gives that store's corner. The paper itself, business_the_chicago_democrat, still stands at the crossing in this register because the only printing of the move IT carries is 1835-08-05, five weeks outside the scene; joining the two records is T-0411's and is deliberately not done here.

changes.from: the corner of Franklin and South Water streets

anchor_change.rule: Giles Spring's office card is reset once. From 1833-12-17 to 1834-11-26 every printing sets the office 'second door west from the corner of Franklin and South Water streets', on the copy date 17 December 1833. From 1835-05-20 the card is a different one — copy-dated 3 December 1834, seven days after the last printing of the old address — and it reads 'OFFICE, first door north from the Tremont House, on Dearborn-street'. These are two crossings of this town and not two spellings of one: Franklin and South Water is on the river's south bank at the west end of the business row, and the first Tremont House stands at the north-west corner of Lake and Dearborn, some four blocks east of it. The identity merge of 'Giles Spring' into 'G. Spring' already reads both cards off the page and says the second one moves him; this rule is that reading applied to the placement, not a new judgement. The corpus carries no printing of either card between 1834-11-26 and 1835-05-20, so the change is bracketed by those two dates and no closer — with the copy date of 3 December 1834 saying only when the new card was WRITTEN, which is not the same as when the office moved.
anchor_change.cannot_say: WHEN THE OFFICE ACTUALLY MOVED, AND WHETHER IT MOVED AT ALL. A card copy-dated 3 December 1834 that first appears in this deposit on 20 May 1835 leaves five and a half months in which nothing printed here says where Spring sat; the deposit is not the paper's whole run, so the new address may have been printed weeks or months before the issue that carries it, and the old one may have gone on running beside it in issues this project does not hold. Nor does anything printed say that ONE office moved rather than that a lawyer who had rooms on South Water Street took rooms on Dearborn Street: both would read exactly like this. What the rule decides is only which anchor the card is printed under at the scene date of 1835-07-01 — the Tremont House, first printed 20 May 1835 and printed again 5 August 1835 — and that is a statement about the ADVERTISEMENT. The earlier anchor is kept with its own dates and its own eleven printings so a later pass can still tell a removal from a second office. The Dearborn address is itself a count of doors, 'first door north from the Tremont House': it fixes a side of Dearborn Street and an order along it, not a lot width, and no lot is claimed for it here.

anchor.note: The landmark is the committed structure tremont_house_1.

anchor_change.live_reason: The last of these anchors first printed on or before the scene date 1835-07-01; this one was first printed 1834-09-10.
anchor_change.rule: Between 1834-06-11 and 1834-09-10 the anchor of this standing advertisement changes from "Graves' Tavern" to "the Tremont House" and the rest of the copy does not change with it — same 26 November 1833 copy date, same 'in all its various branches', same shoes and chains, same 'Work done on the shortest notice'. Two different landmarks, and this project holds both: Graves' Tavern is the log tavern modelled as `mansion_house` on the north side of Lake Street just east of Dearborn, and the first Tremont House stands at the north-west corner of the same crossing, some 36 m west of it. They are not two spellings of one house and they are not the same corner. The corpus carries no printing of this advertisement between those two dates, so the change is bracketed by them and no closer.
anchor_change.cannot_say: WHICH SIDE OF THE STREET MOVED. Nothing printed anywhere in this corpus says whether the shop moved along Lake Street, or the house across from it changed hands and name, or a compositor was handed fresh copy for a reason nobody printed. All three would read exactly like this. The scene date is 1835-07-01, ten months after the later reading first ran, so the anchor live at the scene date is the Tremont House — that is a statement about the ADVERTISEMENT and not about the building, and the earlier anchor is kept with its own dates so a later pass can still tell the two cases apart. The reconstruction's own placement of `mason_blacksmith_shop` was set opposite `mansion_house` on the strength of the 1833-11-26 printing alone, and it has not been moved here: moving it would decide the question this note exists to leave open.

anchor_change.live_anchor: the corner of South Water and Clark streets
anchor_change.live_reason: The last of these anchors first printed on or before the scene date 1835-07-01; this one was first printed 1833-11-26.

changes.from: the corner of South Water and Clark streets

anchor_change.rule: THE SAME MOVE AS THE COLOPHON'S, WITNESSED FIVE WEEKS TOO LATE TO PLACE THIS RECORD. Every reading of the paper's own imprint through 1834-12-03 gives 'the corner of South Water and Clark streets'; 1835-08-05 c026 gives "Jones & King's hardware store". Two different landmarks, bracketed between 1834-12-03 and 1835-08-05 — a platted crossing and a house of business in South Water Street, and a paper is not printed at both. The change is real and this rule states it. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO IS PLACE THIS RECORD ON IT. The later anchor was first printed 1835-08-05, five weeks after the scene date 1835-07-01, and AGENTS.md rule 3 refuses an address to a town that had not read it yet; the compiler computes the live anchor from the windows and leaves this record at the crossing for that reason alone, which is what `live_reason` says. This declaration exists so that the reason is IN the record: before it, this house sat at the corner with nothing to say that its own paper had printed a different address, and a reader could only find that out by reading business_chicago_democrat_printing_office.
anchor_change.cannot_say: WHETHER THE SCENE BOUND IS RIGHT ABOUT THIS HOUSE, and the corpus is in two minds because it keeps the Democrat as two records. The paper's own printing office carries the same move from 1835-05-20, six weeks INSIDE the scene, and is placed on it; this record's only printing of it is 1835-08-05 and is refused. So on 1835-07-01 the register stands the office over the hardware store and the paper at the crossing, which is not two premises but two extractions of one shop — the relation the gazetteer cannot express and T-0411 is open on. Nothing here forces them together: merging on the strength of this would decide T-0411 by side effect, and weakening the scene bound to let an August printing place a July town would decide it for every house in the corpus. NOR DOES IT SAY WHICH SIDE MOVED — 1835-08-05 is a fire-insurance card and the corner readings are a masthead, so the two are not even the same kind of statement about an address, and nothing printed says whether the press moved, the building changed hands, or a compositor was handed fresh copy.
